pr.title: Refactor move analysis subpath representation
pr.description:
Follow up to rust-lang/rust#147055

This PR does two things:
1. Document/validate move analysis's assumptions about `Subslice` projections
2. Decouple move paths from `ProjectionElem`, using a new enum `MoveSubPath` instead
    - This would be needed eventually when `ProjectionElem::Deref` is removed

I wanted to do even more abstraction, making `MovePathLookup::find` return an iterator to remove the special handling of subslices in borrowck, but that regressed diagnostics and just wasn't worth the complexity.
pr.author: beepster4096

processing.reason: No source-grounded original/incorrect pair can be validated for this PR. The patch only (1) strengthens the MIR Validator to reject malformed Index/ConstantIndex/Subslice projections that the old validator accepted, and (2) refactors move-path bookkeeping from ProjectionKind keys to MoveSubPath keys, preserving the existing array-Subslice-to-ConstantIndex splitting for slice-pattern moves. It supplies no runtime regression test or codegen transformation: the material contains no src/test changes and the decoded MIR diff layer is empty. The historical behavior is acceptance of ill-formed MIR (e.g. from_end indexing of arrays, out-of-bounds ConstantIndex, Subslice followed by ConstantIndex), which cannot be produced by ordinary well-typed Rust under Miri without constructing custom MIR. The move-path representation changes also do not alter any concrete numeric/boolean/character result for valid programs; they only change internal path identity/disjointness. Modeling the old-vs-new validator predicate on a hand-built invalid projection descriptor would test a validation predicate, not an actual wrong value-producing transformation, and would violate the requirement not to manufacture an unrelated rewrite just to obtain a difference. Therefore no legitimate test_program_pair exists for this refactor/hardening PR.

analysis.summary: This is a validation-hardening/refactor PR rather than a confirmed miscompile fix. It introduces `MoveSubPath` for move-path projections and strengthens the MIR `Validator` to reject malformed `Index`/`ConstantIndex`/`Subslice` projections and to enforce that, before runtime MIR, a `Subslice` is not followed by `ConstantIndex` or another `Subslice`. Move analysis must expand an array `Subslice` into disjoint per-element `ConstantIndex` move paths because drop elaboration expects disjoint paths.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this patch, the `Validator` checked `Deref` by MIR phase, rejected `OpaqueCast` after `Runtime(RuntimePhase::Initial)`, and checked that an `Index` local had type `usize`, but it did not validate the indexed place type or the shape/bounds/`from_end` form of `ConstantIndex` and `Subslice`, nor reject `ConstantIndex`/`Subslice` after `Subslice` before runtime MIR. Move paths stored and looked up projections directly by `ProjectionKind`, and `gather_move` had a special branch that split a trailing `ProjectionElem::Subslice { from, to, from_end: false }` into `ConstantIndex` move paths.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The pre-change logic accepted place projection sequences that the new validator rejects: `Index`/`ConstantIndex`/`Subslice` applied to a non-array/non-slice type, arrays indexed or subsliced `from_end: true`, slices subsliced with `from_end: false`, a `ConstantIndex` whose offset is out of bounds of `min_length`, a backwards `from_end: false` subslice, and, before runtime MIR, `ConstantIndex` or `Subslice` appearing after `Subslice`. Its move-path representation also used raw `ProjectionKind` keys and only expanded a `Subslice` in the final projection position during `gather_move`. No confirmed miscompile is established by this PR; these are the old behaviors replaced by the refactor and its new validation.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR places and projections over locals of array, slice, ADT, closure, coroutine, and tuple types; projection elements `Index`, `ConstantIndex`, `Subslice`, `Field`, `Downcast`, `Deref`, `OpaqueCast`, and `UnwrapUnsafeBinder`; bodies before and after `MirPhase::Runtime(RuntimePhase::Initial)`; move paths created for moves, overwrites, drops, and slice-pattern moves, especially array slice patterns.
analysis.trigger: When constructing, transforming, or validating MIR place projections before runtime MIR, especially array slice patterns and `Subslice` projections; or when changing how move-analysis subpaths are represented or looked up.
preconditions: The checked body phase is before `MirPhase::Runtime(RuntimePhase::Initial)` when enforcing the no-`ConstantIndex`/`Subslice`-after-`Subslice` rule.
The `Subslice` being expanded by move analysis is `from_end: false` over a fixed-size array; slice subslices are not movable-through subpaths.
The place has a well-typed base and projection sequence so `place_ref.ty(...)` can determine the type before each projection.
For array slice-pattern moves, `Subslice { from, to, from_end: false }` is expanded into `ConstantIndex` children so move paths stay disjoint for drop elaboration.
pitfalls: Do not treat `Subslice` as one move path; split it into per-element `ConstantIndex` subpaths because drop elaboration expects disjoint move paths.
`from_end: true` `ConstantIndex` and `Subslice` are not movable-through; `Index` is also a stop for move-path lookup.
`OpaqueCast` is skipped by move-path lookup, not turned into a child move path.
`ConstantIndex` bounds differ by direction: `offset >= min_length` fails when `from_end` is false, while `offset > min_length` fails when `from_end` is true.
Arrays must not be indexed or subsliced from the end; slices must be subsliced from the end when using `Subslice`.
Only `from_end: false` subslices are checked for backwards (`from > to`) ranges.
Do not conflate rejecting invalid MIR with proving an optimization miscompiled; this patch adds validation and refactoring without a supplied regression test.
analysis.testStrategy: For `Validator`-focused tests, build or mutate MIR bodies at phases before `Runtime(Initial)` with one projection condition at a time and assert the expected validation failure: `Subslice` followed by `ConstantIndex`/`Subslice`; `Index` on a non-array/non-slice type; array with `from_end: true`; slice with `Subslice { from_end: false }`; out-of-bounds `ConstantIndex` using both `>=` and `>` rules; backwards `from_end: false` subslice; and valid controls for array subslice and slice from-end subslice. For move-analysis behavior, use array slice-pattern moves and checks that each element receives a `ConstantIndex` move path and that paths are disjoint, with `OpaqueCast` skipped and `Index`/from-end projections stopping lookup. Do not claim execution or reproduction; no compiler was built.
